content: This medication, zidovudine, is known to pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to note that this document does not include all possible drug interactions. You should maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect how zidovudine is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. This medication should not be taken with other drugs that contain zidovudine. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as blood counts, liver function tests, viral load, and T-cell counts, are necessary to monitor your condition. It is crucial to keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Zidovudine has been associated with severe blood problems, including anemia (a decrease in red blood cells) and neutropenia (a decrease in white blood cells). These issues are more common in individuals with advanced HIV disease (AIDS) and may require blood transfusions or discontinuation of the medication. Your doctor will order blood tests to monitor for these complications. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of anemia, such as unusual fatigue, difficulty breathing, weakness, bluish fingernails or lips, pale skin, or a rapid heartbeat. Low white blood cell counts can increase your risk of serious, potentially fatal infections. This medication may also cause muscle problems (myopathy). Rarely, zidovudine has been linked to severe, sometimes fatal liver problems and a metabolic condition called lactic acidosis. Seek medical help immediately if you develop symptoms of liver problems, such as persistent nausea, abdominal pain, dark urine, or yellowing of the eyes or skin, or symptoms of lactic acidosis, such as rapid breathing, drowsiness, or muscle aches. Zidovudine is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This reduces the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. Zidovudine is also used in pregnant women to prevent the transmission of HIV to the unborn baby. However, it is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually 2 to 3 times daily. Swallow it with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise instructed. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also based on weight. Pregnant women may need to take this medication 5 times a day. Take zidovudine 2 hours before or after taking clarithromycin. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is essential to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, take more or less than prescribed, or stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval. Common side effects may include headache, nausea, vomiting, difficulty sleeping, or loss of appetite. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Loss of body fat (such as in the face, arms, legs, and buttocks) may occur while taking this medication, and this effect may be permanent. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking zidovudine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Liquid products may contain sugar, so caution is advised if you have diabetes or any condition requiring you to limit sugar intake. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of zidovudine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. This medication must not be taken with other drugs containing zidovudine.
